newsitem.title: UK: Commodity Fund approve cocoa, coffee, zinc finance.
newsitem.headline: Commodity Fund approve cocoa, coffee, zinc finance.

text.p: At a meeting in the Hague this week the Executive Board of the Common Fund for Commodities (CFC) approved a total $10.6 million to be directed towards financing various cocoa, coffee and zinc cotton projects.

In a press release the CFC said this represented 41 percent of the total project costs. It brought the total number of projects supported by the CFC to 50 and the total value of all projects to about $120 million.

Cocoa projects included the development of new cocoa plant varieties to fight Witches' Broom Disease, which is devastating some cocoa plantations, and lower cost production of cocoa more resistant to some of the major diseases and pests.

Coffee will benefit from financing for the fight against Coffee Berry Borer which has become a major pest in more than forty coffee growing countries all over the world. Also, the CFC will help fund a study of marketing and trading policies in selected coffee producing countries.
Money will also be directed towards the expansion of zinc demand by introducing modern techniques of zinc die-casting and galvanising to developing countries.

The CFC will also help fund the fight against cotton stickiness, which reduces the quality of yarn, and to improve the declining productivity of coconut which is losing its competitiveness on world markets.
